claims: Artemis I launched on November 16, 2022.
Artemis I launched at 1:47 a.m. EST.
Artemis I launched from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
Artemis I was an uncrewed flight test.
Artemis I utilized the Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1 rocket.
Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1 is the world’s most powerful rocket.
Artemis I sent the Orion spacecraft around the Moon.
Artemis I lasted 25 days, 10 hours, and 53 minutes.
Artemis I splashed down on December 11, 2022.
Launch vehicle for Artemis I was Space Launch System (SLS) Block 1.
Payload for Artemis I was uncrewed Orion capsule.
Objective of Artemis I was to test the integrated systems of SLS and Orion for future crewed missions.
Artemis I launch occurred after several delays caused by tropical storms.
Artemis I launch occurred after several delays caused by hydrogen fuel leaks during previous countdown attempts.
Artemis I traveled approximately 1.4 million miles.
Artemis I reached a record distance of 270,000 miles from Earth.
Orion capsule survived reentry at ~24,581 mph.
Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean.
Artemis II is scheduled for 2026.
Artemis II will carry four astronauts around the Moon.
Artemis III is planned to land the first woman and next man on the Moon.
